subject: Nightshift GPU corridor — temporary reserve & autoscale exception proposal
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Nightshift GPU corridor — temporary reserve & autoscale exception proposal

Team,

Quick ask: product is seeing a steady rise in nightly evaluation jobs for the Atlas pilot (model-sensitivity sweeps). These are low-priority, long-running batch evals that hit the Dedicated GPU pools between 00:00–06:00 PT and are starting to interfere with our burst lanes for customer-facing requests during early-morning APAC activity.

Proposal: create a time-windowed temporary reserve — a "nightshift corridor" — for the next 4 weeks (June 25 → July 22) that guarantees up to 8 A100-equivalent GPUs from 00:00–05:30 PT for evals, with an autoscale exception to avoid preemption during long sweeps. We want this to be a temporary carveout, automatically revoked after the window unless renewed.

Attached is a matrix showing job counts and proposed sizing by weekday. Key asks for infra/ops:
- Confirm feasibility of a time-bound carveout and the simplest implementation path (reservation vs. policy-based timeslot).
- Estimate the impact on other customers if we hold 8 GPUs nightly for four weeks.
- Approve an autoscale exception so these jobs are not evicted mid-sweep (we can accept soft-fallback to lower-precision variants if capacity is tight).

Why temporary: we want to run this controlled window to gather signal on cost/latency tradeoffs before requesting a standing slice for Atlas.

Attachments: nightshift_reserve_matrix.xlsx (matrix + job histogram)

Vanessa
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightshift GPU corridor — temporary reserve & autoscale exception proposal

Vanessa — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. A few clarifying questions from infra:

1) Narrow the window: you called out 00:00–05:30 PT (5.5 hrs). Is traffic concentrated in the 00:00–03:30 PT slice? If we can concentrate to a shorter window we can reduce prime-time risk.
2) Job profile: are these single-GPU jobs or multi-GPU? The matrix shows "job-hours" but not concurrency.
3) Autoscale exception scope: do you want to exempt from preemption but still allow bursting above the reserved 8 GPUs if free capacity exists, or should those jobs strictly be limited to the reserved corridor?

Operational constraints to flag: an exception that prevents preemption for long-running jobs increases interference risk with latency SLO customers during unusual spikes. If we do this, we should:
- limit the exception to the listed project tag (atlas-evals-night)
- cap the per-job GPU count to 2 unless a product sign-off is given for specific runs
- require a daily capacity report to infra (CSV) showing actual usage vs. reserved.

I can prototype a policy-based timeslot (preferred) by EOD Wed if you can confirm job concurrency and the exact hours. If we need hard reservations, that will require a short procurement ticket and will take 48–72 hrs to enforce across clusters.

—Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightshift GPU corridor — temporary reserve & autoscale exception proposal

Adding ops perspective. Short version: doable, but we need explicit runbook steps and an eviction fallback in case cluster health degrades.

Notes / constraints:
- Time-window reservations are the least invasive: we mark a policy that routes atlas-evals-night to a reserved slice during the hours. Implementation: ~6–8 hours ops work + a safety toggle that can be flipped on/off from the Console.
- Hard carveouts at the allocation layer will reduce flexibility for cross-region failover and will require a procurement/finance sign-off if it becomes recurring.
- We should gate the autoscale exception behind a daily usage digest and a runbook entry (attach). I put a draft runbook in the drive (ops_runbook_nightcorridor.pdf).

Suggested mitigations:
- Soft fallback: if queue depth for latency-critical pools exceeds threshold X for >10 minutes, the system may preempt oldest atlas-evals-night jobs with a notification channel to SRE and Product.
- Canary week: roll this in for one week at 50% capacity (4 GPUs) to measure external impact before scaling to 8.

I can schedule the change for week-of June 25 if product approves the canary plan.

Marcus
Principal, Cloud Ops
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightshift GPU corridor — temporary reserve & autoscale exception proposal

Thanks — I pulled the matrix and did a quick customer-impact analysis. A few product-level considerations: 

- Risk: Even though this is nightly, APAC customers surface issues early in their day. We need to ensure that 8 GPUs doesn't increase tail latency for request paths that slide into those pools. If the canary week shows any tail-latency drift we should abort.
- Success metric: keep 95th percentile request latency within +5% of baseline and keep infra cost delta <15% for the 4-week window.
- Observability: add a per-model latency check and token-cost delta to the Console dashboard for the corridor. If the metric crosses threshold we auto-disable the exception.

As for autoscale exception: product is comfortable with a soft exception. In other words: prevent preemption for the first 30 minutes of a job, after which it becomes preemptible if cluster pressure spikes beyond the defined threshold. That reduces the risk of very long-running non-interactive jobs monopolizing resources.

Grace
Sr PM, Dedicated Products
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightshift GPU corridor — temporary reserve & autoscale exception proposal

Soojin — can you approve the temporary policy-change to enable a week-long canary starting June 25 for 4 GPUs (00:00–04:00 PT)?

Plan summary (canary):
- Duration: June 25–July 1
- Size: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs nightly (00:00–04:00 PT)
- Autoscale policy: soft exception — non-preemptible for first 30 minutes, preemptible thereafter if latency-critical pools breach threshold X
- Controls: ops runbook in Drive + daily usage CSV to infra + dashboard alerts (95th latency, token-cost delta) that auto-disable the policy on breach
- Post-canoiry: run a short retro and if signal is clean we escalate to the full 8-GPU window for the remaining three weeks.

Attachments: nightshift_reserve_matrix.xlsx, ops_runbook_nightcorridor.pdf

If approved, Aditya/Marcus: please implement the policy toggle and the alert hooks. I will notify EchoHealth (Alice) and our cloud partner (Sam) that this is internal-only and temporary.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Director, Product Ops
